title: Chapter 116 — The Dying Whale
paragraphs: Not seldom in this life, when, on the right side, fortune's favorites sail close by us, we, though all drooping before, catch somewhat of the rushing breeze and joyfully feel our sagging sails fill out. So it seemed with the Pequod. For next day after encountering the gay Bachelor, whales were seen and four were slain; and one of them by Ahab.

It was far down the afternoon; and when all the spearings of the crimson fight were done, and floating in the lovely sunset sea and sky, sun and whale both stilly died together — then such a sweetness and such plaintiveness, such entwining prayers curled up in that rosy air, that it almost seemed as if far over from the deep green valley-lands there came that gentle shout over the world-renowned calf-pastures, "Our Jenny's dead."

Soothed again, but only soothed to deeper gloom, Ahab, who had backed off from the whale, sat intently watching its final wanings from the now tranquil boat. For that strange spectacle observable in all sperm whales dying — the turning sunward of the head, and so expiring — that strange spectacle, beheld in such benign evening weather, somehow conveyed to Ahab a wondrousness unknown before.

"He turns and turns to it — how slowly, but how steadfastly, his homage-rendering and invoking brow, with his last dying motions. He too worships fire; most faithful, broad, baronial vassal of the sun! Oh that these too-favoring eyes should see these too-favoring sights. Look! Here, far water-locked; beyond all hum of human weal or woe; in these most candid and impartial seas; where to traditions no rocks furnish tablets; where for long Chinese ages the billows have still rolled on speechless and unspoken to, as stars that shine upon the Niger's unknown source — here, too, life dies sunward."

"Oh, you dark Hindu half of nature, who of drowned bones have built your separate throne somewhere in the heart of these unverdured seas; you are an infidel, you queen, and too truly you speak to me in the wide-slaughtering Typhoon, and the hushed burial of its after-calm. Nor has this your whale sunward turned his dying head, and then gone round again, without the lesson to me."

"Oh, trebly hooped and welded hip of power! Oh, high aspiring, rainbowed jet! The one strives, the other jets, all in vain! In vain, oh whale, do you seek intercession with the all-quickening sun, that only calls forth life but gives it not again. Yet do you, darker half, rock me with a prouder, if a darker faith. All your unnamable inmixings float beneath me here; I am buoyed by breaths of once living things, exhaled as air, but water now."

"Then hail, forever hail, O sea, in whose eternal tossings the wild fowl finds his only rest. Born of earth, yet suckled by the sea; though hill and valley mothered me, you billows are my foster-brothers!"
